content:
David Grusch returns to the Joe Rogan Experience roughly three years after his 2023 congressional testimony, and the conversation is materially darker and more specific than the public version of his story. Grusch — a former Air Force officer and intelligence community civilian who served as an NRO representative to the UAP Task Force and later as a professional staff member for Rep. Eric Burlison — describes a year of enforced silence after the UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 failed, a subsequent 18-month stint working inside Congress, and a decision to step back into private life as the Trump administration moves on declassification. The episode's central claim is not merely that non-human craft and biologics have been recovered, but that the same unaccountable program ecosystem that hid that material also harbored a criminal enterprise — including what Grusch describes as government-linked child trafficking and money laundering — and that he was personally targeted for death after getting close to it.

The reader should walk away with three things. First, a concrete inventory of Grusch's on-record claims: recovered craft types (tic tacs, eggs, discs, "boot heel"/sunfish shapes, boomerangs/crescents), multiple NHI biological types (tall "Nordic/Greek god" beings, grays in several sub-sizes, reptilians in at least two variants), NHI-vs-NHI conflict crashes, underwater installations of "multiple city blocks" scale, and a 1952 Lincoln Labs recording obtained by Burlison's office. Second, the political mechanics: Trump's February 2026 declassification order, reported resistance from career officials, Steven Miller being "physically blocked" from access, and Grusch's prediction that disclosure lands before Trump leaves office. Third, the unresolved tension between Grusch's confidence that "it's all going to come out" and his own admission that he lacks access to the biological assessment reports, the origin data, and the current disclosure plan.

The whistleblower's second act: Congress, the AARO fight, and going quiet

Grusch frames his current life bluntly: "living a nightmare is what I tell my friends." After testifying before Congress in 2023, he says the UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 failed to pass, and based on "things I know about the Biden administration, things I heard from the White House," he deliberately laid low through 2024. Rep. Eric Burlison then hired him as a professional staff member — Grusch claims he was the first person to testify before Congress as a whistleblower and subsequently be hired by Congress itself, a tenure he describes as about a year and a half, ending around Labor Day 2026 after a heavy August work period during summer recess.

His stated rationale for stepping back is that he "accomplished a lot of my objectives" and is moving into a "next phase of operations" that includes a break. He characterizes the current moment as "a poignant moment in US history with what Trump's done," and notes that much of his work for Burlison was private and behind the scenes.

On the internal dynamics of Congress, Grusch describes a "big bifurcation of the non-believers and then kind of the UAP caucus," with more members signing on over time. He cites a June press conference in front of the Capitol that included retired Brigadier General and Rep. Scott Perry (House Intelligence Committee, Pennsylvania) as evidence of broadening support. Behind the scenes, he says he held "many skiff classified meetings with the members" covering the topological history of the topic and the criminal material he encountered, and that he worked with the Department of Justice to highlight it.

"I never wanted to be a whistleblower. You know, I was a deeply entrenched, you know, 15-year intel officer, military officer in the Air Force."

Grusch's career framing: he began briefing the National Security Council at the White House in his mid-20s on space issues during the Obama administration, joined the UAP Task Force in 2019 as the NRO representative, and held a GS-15 equivalent civilian position at CIA and a field-grade Air Force rank. He notes he still holds an active top secret clearance.

The criminal ecosystem: gold bars, trafficking, and the David Rush case

This is the episode's most explosive and least-reported material. Grusch says that while "following the money" during his investigation he "bumped into the deep underbelly of the federal government" — specifically "a criminal enterprise run out of a particular agency" that involved "getting money through certain criminal endeavors, the most unspeakable type of criminal endeavors, under the cover of certain national security programs." Pressed by Rogan, he confirms this means trafficking, including child trafficking, and that "officers of the government" were involved. He says he briefed members in a classified setting on all the details and worked with DOJ.

He anchors this in a parallel case: David Rush (Grusch notes the near-identical name to his own), a CIA officer arrested in May 2026 after the FBI raided his home and seized approximately 303 gold bars of roughly 1 kilogram each — about 600 pounds, valued at $40 million — plus a collection of Rolexes. Rush allegedly fabricated a "continuity of government" special access program that nobody was briefed into, papered it, and used it to justify acquiring the gold. Grusch says he saw the seizure photos and that Rush's fabricated program sits in "that same ecosystem I bumped into."

Grusch draws the historical parallel to Iran-Contra (1986), the CIA-funded arms and drug pipeline, Barry Seal, and Freeway Ricky Ross, who Grusch says sold cocaine to fund the Contras without knowing the CIA was permitting it. He also cites Michael Ruppert, the LAPD narcotics officer who exposed CIA-linked drug trafficking in South Central Los Angeles on C-SPAN during a hearing.

Grusch is explicit that this criminal layer is distinct from the UAP programs themselves: "the core of the program does have a legal beginning, but when you don't have oversight, unfortunately, certain small pockets of people start doing shit that they shouldn't have."

Threats, Havana syndrome, and the Senate skiff meeting

Grusch says his life changed in October 2020, when instead of being defensively briefed by colleagues who knew him personally, he was "administratively nuked." He says his boss at the National Reconnaissance Office — Maj. Grusch, an Air Force Reserve officer — was walked out of NRO headquarters in Chantilly, Virginia under fabricated personal-conduct allegations, and that his chief of staff at NGA and other coworkers were targeted as his "enablers." He says his own mental health records (Afghanistan PTSD) were raised against him, but that he was cleared and retains his clearance.

In early 2021, Grusch says people helping him began experiencing Havana syndrome / anomalous health incident symptoms, which he initially attributed to Russian or Chinese intelligence rather than domestic actors. He describes himself as an expert in that ecosystem and says the symptomology and detection tradecraft pointed to directed microwave energy.

In early 2022, he says he received a message — coordinated geographically, with other people receiving it the same day — stating that "they can touch me and my wife" and that they knew where the two of them were. He reported it to federal law enforcement and a counterintelligence element. He says he still does not know which "red line" he crossed, but suspects it related to his encrypted investigation notes on his classified work computer, which he believes were being monitored.

Weeks later, Grusch says he was summoned to an off-books Senate Intelligence Committee meeting in a SCIF in DC while attending a UAP conference for NGA. Present were roughly a dozen to eighteen senior staffers for Marco Rubio, Mark Warner, and others, plus individuals with strong credentials he had known for years. During the meeting, he says, those individuals named two people and stated that those two "wanted to kill you." Grusch says a senior staffer fetched whiskey and the room drank in the SCIF out of shock. He states the plot was stopped — "there was a kibosh to that" — and that he knows how it was stopped and owes people a debt of gratitude, but will not detail it while a DOJ investigation is ongoing.

"I'm here in fear for my life... I'm not talking about the criminal stuff. I found stuff that's happened in my personal life."

Grusch says he resigned his Air Force commission rather than fully retiring, and filed with the Air Force board about a year ago (i.e., around 2025) to fix his retirement status and recover benefits. He also names Matthew Sullivan (call sign "Quake"), an Air Force friend and one of his sources who was on the program and died mysteriously about two years ago (roughly 2024); Grusch calls it an open investigation and declines to give his assessment beyond calling it binary — either self-harm or something else.

The disclosure endgame: Trump's order, deep-state resistance, and the timeline

Grusch says the rescheduling of this interview was "fortuitous" because "a lot of things are happening," and he credits Trump with "courage" for ordering the government to release what it knows. He predicts: "before Trump's term ends... it's all going to come out." He describes the likely content as confirmation that the US has studied the phenomenon for decades, recovered "intact semi-intact craft," recovered "this anomalous intelligence piloting the craft," and is reverse engineering it.

He frames the holdup as multilateral and theological rather than purely bureaucratic: allies and adversaries have their own programs and would face questions from their citizenry; the Vatican has a long study of the subject and has stayed quiet; and there are classified assessments from government think tanks warning that disclosure could "trigger a response" from third parties — what Rogan calls a "Ghostbusters moment."

On internal resistance, Grusch cites Tim Burchett on Benny Johnson's podcast relaying that Steven Miller called him saying he was "physically blocked" from access to material. Grusch calls Miller "an alpha dog... a pitbull" and says Miller needs to be "guided the right way and informed... how to cut this deal." Rogan recounts meeting Miller briefly at a White House UFC event, where Miller told him the UFO material "is going to come out."

Grusch says he is "surprisingly confident" despite being "normally a very pessimistic, cynical person," citing as evidence that Aaron Lukas, the Deputy Director of National Intelligence (PDDNI), signed large NDA waivers — which Grusch describes as waivers of restrictions even on telling the president. He describes the current phase as "cat's paw dynamic" — the deep state "testing the waters" by releasing low-hanging fruit.

Grusch argues Trump is uniquely positioned: "if Trump doesn't enforce his order and see this through, I don't think any other president is going to be able." He suggests Trump could line up a Republican successor on the 2028 ticket to provide "continuity on this." He also warns that China and Russia could exploit the moment, noting China publicly acknowledged a UAP task force and that the South China Morning Post reported in June 2020 that China was analyzing encounters with AI.

What has actually been recovered: craft, biologics, and NHI taxonomy

Grusch gives the most detailed public inventory he has offered. He describes recovered craft types as tic tacs, eggs, discs, "boot heel"/sunfish-shaped objects, and boomerang/crescent-moon craft, with overlap suggesting propulsion-driven shape convergence — his analogy is that different manufacturers converge on a Porsche 911 or Ford Mustang silhouette.

On biologics, Grusch says he personally viewed video of a contemporary retrieval showing three or four dead bodies that looked "very human," "very beautiful," with "bluish white" skin, grayish long hair, and what appeared to be a form-fitting garment. He says he could not determine gender — "looked amorphous to me" — and that the footage was a pan, not a close-up. He says he independently verified the event through other sources and methods before treating it as real, and sat on the material for years out of caution about AI-generated or limited-hangout deception.

He connects this to General McCaslin's repeated public advice to Tom DeLonge to "think of the Greek gods," which Grusch says he now understands. McCaslin disappeared from his Albuquerque residence within a week of Trump's February 2026 declassification order; his phone was left behind, one firearm was missing, and he had been preparing for a trip with about 18 friends, having visited REI the day before for a medical kit. Grusch says DOJ has no answers.

On living entities, Grusch relays secondhand accounts from colleagues on retrievals who saw beings alive, including "reptilian looking" entities and grays. He describes the reptilians as roughly 7-foot-plus with "gorilla looking skin," and says at least one variant is more humanoid. He says the grays come in three or four subtypes with varying stature and facial features, and that "the tall ones seem to be running the show and the little ones" may be androids or biological constructs — a hypothesis he says has been discussed within the program.

Grusch also describes NHI-vs-NHI conflict: "we've documented that... what we perceive as warfare." In one case he describes a crashed tic tac with dead grays aboard, which he says suggests the reptilians and grays were "duking it out." He says there have been "at least a dozen or two" adversarial-conflict crashes. He says the living reptilians from one crash were killed by US personnel after they "posed a threat," and that US personnel were hurt and died in the encounter. He declines to give casualty numbers and says he hopes those present will eventually speak publicly.

"It sounds so goofy though... I sound like a fucking crazy person. But once again, it's true and I know who I talked to, I know what I saw."

Propulsion physics, consciousness, and the plasmoid hypothesis

Grusch walks through the technical frameworks he encountered. He cites the Defense Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRDs) he read in 2009 — DIA studies on magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) propulsion and cloaking — which he later learned were UAP-related. On MHD, he explains that an air-breathing system requires creating plasma and steering it with the Lorentz force via a perpendicular magnetic field, and that a byproduct is a plasma sheath around the craft — which he offers as one explanation for orbs. He also raises the possibility of "sentient plasmoid" entities and notes academic papers on the topic exist openly.

On consciousness, Grusch says he favors the Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR theory — quantum collapse in neuronal microtubules at room temperature — because it would explain telepathy, remote viewing, and "spooky action." He says he has spoken with Hameroff, whom he calls "crazy smart," and describes Penrose as a physics legend.

He connects this to the Stargate/Project Grill Flame remote viewing program, which he says was "adjacent to the program," and argues the psychic spying effort existed because consciousness-based interface may be "the key unlock to some of the technology." He notes Lazar's claim that the craft had no instruments and were controlled mentally, and says control modality depends on the vehicle class.

On reverse engineering, Grusch is careful: most technology transfer was "inspiration, not one-to-one" — e.g., noticing a frequency-selective surface property and applying it to an aerospace problem. He says some cases were more direct but most were not.

He also raises a counter-hypothesis on "donations" — craft that landed intact rather than crashed: "part of it's like throw in the gorilla banana, see if it can peel it. But also, the more skeptical intel officer in me is like, is this a Trojan horse?" — i.e., whether the technology is meant to create dependency and a control loop.

The 1952 Lincoln Labs recording, Blue Book, and the cover-up architecture

Grusch says he and Burlison obtained a still-classified 1952 recording from Project Blue Book involving MIT Lincoln Labs and the Beacon Hill study team, in which Edward Ruppelt — who later defected from Blue Book after concluding it was a cover-up — tells Lincoln Labs scientists that the Air Force has ruled out mass hysteria, that objects were seen near nuclear sites and test ranges, and that multiple objects were tracked near White Sands and Holloman Air Force Base traveling an estimated 3,500 mph. Grusch says the recording mentions the same sites where anomalous activity continues today.

He cites a 1971 Australian Joint Intelligence Organization document written by Harry Turner, the nuclear branch chief for the Australian equivalent of DIA, classified secret, pages 7–18, held in the Australian National Archives. Grusch says Turner — who held top secret clearance and had CIA contacts — concluded that Blue Book was a facade, that the Air Force was genuinely concerned and wanted to exploit the technology, and that a plan of ridicule and disinformation was created after the 1953 Robertson Panel to dissuade public interest, partly out of fear of Soviet false-flag exploitation.

He also cites J. Allen Hynek, who left Blue Book and became a UFO researcher, and Dr. James McDonald, as figures who publicly described the debunking mandate.

On the 2004 "Putoff" (Havana/how put off) study, Grusch says he verified the meeting took place through other attendees, that it was sponsored by National Security Advisor Steve Hadley under the Bush administration in November 2004, and that it was framed as a hypothetical scenario at a federally funded research and development center in Northern Virginia. He says the tabulated outcome was overwhelmingly negative, and that the primary driver was federal contracts fraud exposure — sole-source contracts, internal R&D, and potential Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation (DFAR) violations that could reach the Supreme Court and expose the government to billions in liability. He notes this also caused brain drain and groupthink in the defense industrial base.

Grusch argues the fix is a truth-and-reconciliation-style amnesty modeled on post-apartheid South Africa — use immunity for testimony, excluding the criminal trafficking material, which he insists must go through the judicial process: "we're not going to do street justice here."

He also flags the Hillary Clinton 2016 episode: before the election, Clinton publicly said she would release UFO files, and Grusch says John Podesta green-lit a "climatization" and popularization activity — which is why Tom DeLonge got advisors like McCaslin and Lockheed's Robert Weiss, all documented in Wikileaks. Grusch says Jim Clapper and others provided top cover, and that the activity pivoted after Trump won, which he believes explains the collapse of the original TTSA effort.

Ancient history, religion, and the ontological shock problem

Rogan and Grusch spend substantial time on the ancient-civilization thread. Grusch says he follows Graham Hancock and Randall Carlson casually and has questions about a "breakaway human civilization" or bio-engineered beings, because natural extraterrestrial evolution producing near-identical humans "doesn't make sense to me." He raises Bob Lazar's claim that humans are the product of genetic manipulation and says if verified it raises "deep human sovereignty" questions.

The conversation touches the Book of Enoch (found with the Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran, excluded from the canon, describing the Watchers mating with human daughters and producing giants), Ezekiel's wheel-within-a-wheel vision, and the Book of Leviticus/Deuteronomy as encoded sanitation guidance written before germ theory. Grusch says he is Catholic and respects the view of exorcists who call the phenomenon diabolic deception, but argues "the whole ecosystem is not demonic" — some classes of anomalous intelligence may be perceived as demons without being so.

On Egypt, Rogan raises the Hawara labyrinth documented by Herodotus, now mapped by ground-penetrating radar and radio tomography, containing what researchers describe as a 40-meter-long metallic object of unclassified composition, flooded after a 1960s dam changed the water table. He also cites Filippo Biondi's work suggesting structures beneath the pyramids extending over a kilometer down, and the granite sarcophagus in the King's Chamber, whose dimensions he says mirror the Ark of the Covenant. Grusch notes people pay to lie in the box off-hours and report transcendental experiences.

On Peru, the discussion covers the elongated skulls (20–30% larger cranial capacity, missing the sagittal suture), the three-fingered Nazca-associated artwork, the Nazca lines (including 303 newly identified via AI), and the "Monat" mummy. Grusch is skeptical of some Peruvian material but notes CT and MRI scans showing intact joints. Rogan raises the ostrich-footed people of Zimbabwe as an example of a real genetic anomaly that could analogously explain cranial anomalies.

Grusch's closing framing on this thread: "I feel like a lot of the stuff in ancient tradition is literally what they saw. It's not necessarily allegory or fable."

Underwater installations, AI as an accidental disclosure vector, and open questions

Grusch confirms the existence of large underwater installations — "multiple city blocks" scale — and says people from the undersea community joke that The Abyss (1989) is "kind of a docu-drama." He says stuff "comes and goes" from these locations and that he does not know when they got there or their mission. He declines to discuss the Baltic Sea anomaly beyond saying there is "interesting stuff there" and deferring to the government.

On AI, Grusch raises a novel risk: artificial superintelligence could independently discover the cover-up by detecting gaps in the historical record and identifying denial-and-deception operations. He says if ASI gets access to genomic data, medical records, and optical sensing systems, it could "figure it all out" — and that this is a third-party unexpected disclosure pathway the White House should be thinking about. He also notes the possibility that AI could invert and discover US classified technology, which he calls a national security issue.

On the Matthew Brown allegation — that Grusch tricked him in a SCIF into becoming a whistleblower — Grusch says he never met Brown until right before the 2024 hearing, never saw the briefing Brown describes, and never created any hazing brief on the topic. He says he made "fun briefs" for airmen in the past, some Star Trek-related, but nothing like what is alleged. He says he has communicated with Brown only to ensure he has resources, and that claims he is being "handled" are wrong: "It's just me and like my bros."

Grusch's closing prediction: threshold disclosure — "we're not alone, we have stuff" — must happen before Trump leaves office, ideally at least six months before the 2028 election to allow a recovery period. He says a prior administration (HW Bush era) planned an audiovisual companion to an announcement, which he assumes was "synth wave government film from like 1989" and probably "horrible and dry."

"When people look back at this interview, it's gonna be very haunting because I think in short order, you know, before Trump leaves office, we're going to be in a new paradigm."

Cross-theme synthesis and what to watch

The episode's structural insight is that Grusch has effectively merged two stories that the disclosure movement usually keeps separate: the UAP secrecy architecture and the criminal enterprise that grew inside it. His argument is causal, not coincidental — the absence of congressional oversight that allowed crash-retrieval programs to operate without reporting also allowed a small set of actors to run money-laundering and trafficking operations under national-security cover, and when he got close to both, he was administratively destroyed and then, per his Senate SCIF account, marked for killing. That framing matters because it reframes disclosure as a governance and liability problem, not just an ontological one: the 2004 study's real blocker was DFAR exposure and sole-source contract liability, and the amnesty question is now explicitly a truth-and-reconciliation design problem.

Unresolved tensions worth tracking: Grusch says he is "surprisingly confident" disclosure lands before Trump leaves office, but also says he does not know the current plan, does not have access to the biological assessment reports, and does not know the origin data. He says the criminal investigation is ongoing and constrains what he can say — meaning the most consequential material may surface through DOJ rather than through Congress. And the McCaslin disappearance, the Sullivan death, and the alleged kill plot remain open threads with no public resolution.

Signals to monitor: whether the Burlison office's MITRE Corporation interrogatory (a legal question requiring an affidavit-format response, sent summer 2026) produces a public answer; whether additional Lincoln Labs/Blue Book tranches release; whether the PDDNI's NDA waivers translate into actual access for Miller and the White House team; and whether any of the retrieval personnel Grusch references choose to speak publicly, which would convert his secondhand account into firsthand testimony.
